summary.title: As a data scientist what is your best resource of everyday learning?
summary.one_liner: A Quora thread of working data scientists' answers on how they keep learning day to day: blogs, podcasts, arXiv, open-source code, other practitioners, and hands-on projects.
keywords: daily learning routine for data scientists
takeaways: Working on real, messy projects is repeatedly named as the strongest way to learn data science.
Many answers recommend a mix of curated blogs (e.g., Uber Engineering, Airbnb, DataCamp, Dataquest), podcasts, and arXiv papers.
Discussing problems with other data scientists and reading open-source code are cited as valuable everyday learning habits.
One answer offers a structured daily/weekly routine: a core blog or newsletter, fast feeds, 15-30 minutes of hands-on practice, and a weekly deep dive.
Some contributors note that blogs often go inactive, so feeds and communities need periodic checking.
summary.summary: This is a Quora Q&A thread with many answers from practitioners and a grad student about how to learn data science continuously. Answers list specific blogs, podcasts (such as The Super Data Science Podcast), arXiv, Hacker News, Stack Overflow and Cross Validated, GitHub code, and competitions. Several answers stress that hands-on projects and discussion with colleagues beat passive resources. One answer gives a detailed daily, weekly, and monthly learning plan, while others are short personal lists and opinions. The page is a mixed collection of opinions rather than a single structured tutorial.
